hook: 1% dehydration. That's all it takes to measurably impair your working memory.
topic: Hydration and cognitive performance — the most underestimated mechanism
body:
**Losing just one percent of your body weight in fluid — which is mild dehydration, below the threshold of noticeable thirst — measurably impairs working memory, attention, and processing speed.**

One percent of body weight. For most adults, that is less than a kilogram. You lose that through breathing, baseline movement, and the warmth of a normal room, before you ever sit down to work.

This is not a wellness talking point. It is a documented, replicable effect across multiple independent studies. Mild dehydration degrades the precise cognitive capacities that complex work depends on.

The reason this matters is that most people reach for coffee when they feel cognitively slow. Coffee is a mild diuretic. It does not correct dehydration. For a meaningful portion of that morning fog, the correct intervention is 500 millilitres of water — consumed before any other input — and it takes three minutes.

Start there. Before the coffee. Before the protocol. Start there.
